science.label: Volcanic heat
science.description: Juno JIRAM 4.8 µm night side · Mura et al. 2024 scale
science.title: Heat from Io's volcanoes at 4.8 µm, seen by Juno's JIRAM camera on the night side, where no sunlight is reflected. Each spot is a hot spot's glow; the rest of the night side is too cold to register. Color follows the linear scale of Mura et al. (2024), Figure 2. Gray grid: never seen at night by the frames used.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.notes: USGS Voyager/Galileo mosaic on a 1 km grid; original detail varies from about 1 to 10 km per pixel. Gray grid marks documented no-data and its resampled boundary. Photographed terrain shading remains; globe lighting is approximate.

controls.label: False color
controls.notes: USGS false-color mosaic: near-infrared, green and violet color ratios combined with observed monochrome detail. USGS corrected broad limb darkening and matched image seams. Source color detail varies from 1.3 to 21 km per pixel. Interpolated polar color is withheld; observed monochrome remains where available. Gray grid marks missing imagery. Acquisition shading, seams and changes between mission dates can remain; globe lighting is approximate.

controls.label: Geology

legend.title: Geologic units
legend.meta: Symbols identify archived categories. Colors are chosen for this display.

controls.notes: Fourteen base geologic units mapped from Voyager and Galileo observations. Colors distinguish interpreted plains, lava flows, patera floors and mountains. The separate diffuse-deposit overlay and structural linework are not shown. Gray grid marks unmapped or conflicting polygons; this view adds no measured relief.

controls.label: Spectral slope
controls.notes: Slope from 477.5 to 495 nm, normalized at 495 nm, in published VLT/MUSE observations from July 2019. Sulfur materials affect this slope; it is not sulfur-dioxide abundance. Native two-degree samples remain visible. Nights retain differences and seams; gray grid marks missing or conservatively withheld edges. Absolute subpixel registration is unresolved.

controls.label: Visible absorption
controls.notes: Published mean absorption around 560 nm after continuum removal. The 578–605 nm instrument gap is omitted. Sulfur-bearing materials can contribute, but the absorbing species is not uniquely identified. July 2019 observing nights retain seams and residual differences. Native two-degree samples, missing areas and withheld edges remain; this is not abundance.

controls.label: Volcanic heat

facts.label: Quantity
facts.value: Measured M-band (4.5–5.0 µm) radiance, night side

facts.label: Coverage
facts.value: 22% of Io; 34 Juno JIRAM frames, orbits 41–49

controls.notes: Heat from Io's volcanoes at 4.8 µm, our own reduction of 34 Juno JIRAM frames from orbits 41, 43, 47 and 49 (April 2022 to March 2023), the orbits Mura et al. (2024) mapped. Only the night side is kept, where no sunlight is reflected. Each hot spot's total output agrees with the paper's; its peak is lower, because we do not sharpen the images as they do. Color follows the linear scale of their Figure 2. Gray grid: never seen at night in these orbits, including the south and Loki Patera.
